QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_13

question.text: Ms. Kavita Menon, manager of Sahyadri Opportunities AIF, sees tenure expiring on 30-Jun-2026. Under the 2023 SEBI amendments, the 'Liquidation Period' available for selling remaining assets before triggering in-specie distribution is:

answer.text: Until LPs vote otherwise, with no hard cap

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (AIF) (Second Amendment) Regulations 2023 effective 15-Jun-2023, the Liquidation Period is ONE YEAR following expiry of tenure (or extended tenure). Within this period the AIF must fully liquidate assets or propose in-specie distribution (with 75% consent) or enter a Dissolution Period. The Trap: 6 months understates; 2 years confuses with the tenure-extension cap. 'No hard cap' is factually wrong — SEBI explicitly limits the window. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C territory — earlier Distributor exams pre-dated the 2023 Liquidation Period rule. Manager's Pro-Tip: Begin structured exit auctions 18 months before tenure-end, not during liquidation. Once you're in the Liquidation Period, buyers sense urgency and bid discipline erodes — a 10-15% price haircut is typical.
